title: Mortgage Rates, Home Loan Guides & Expert Insights | The Mortgage Reports

items.title: NC Home Advantage Mortgage: North Carolina’s $15,000 Forgivable Down Payment Help
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>North Carolina's NC 1st Home Advantage gives first-time buyers $15,000 at 0%, forgiven in years 11–15. Repeat buyers can get up to 3% through NC Home Advantage. See limits.</article>

items.title: IHDA Down Payment Assistance: Illinois Access Programs Explained
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>IHDA's Access programs give Illinois buyers $6,000 to $10,000 in down payment help, and Access Home offers up to $15,000 to first-time buyers. Compare terms and requirements.</article>

items.title: Citi Lender Paid Assistance and HomeRun Mortgage
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Citi offers eligible buyers up to $7,500 for specified closing costs or a rate buydown in Citi Assessment Areas. Income or census-tract criteria and other requirements apply.</article>

items.title: Wells Fargo Homebuyer Access Grant
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Wells Fargo's Homebuyer Access grant is a $10,000 grant for eligible borrowers in eligible areas, applied in full to the down payment, and its Dream. Plan. Home. credit adds up to $5,000 for closing costs.</article>

items.title: Bank of America Down Payment Grant and America’s Home Grant
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Bank of America's Down Payment Grant gives first-time buyers up to 3% of the price (max $10,000), in select markets. Eligible borrowers may also qualify for up to $7,500 toward specified closing costs or a permanent rate buydown.</article>

items.title: Los Angeles LIPA and MIPA: Up to $161,000 in Loans for First-Time Buyers
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Los Angeles offers eligible buyers deferred purchase-assistance loans with shared appreciation. Compare LIPA and MIPA limits, repayment rules and reservation dates.</article>

items.title: Utah Down Payment Assistance by City and County
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Utah Housing lends up to 6% of your loan for down payment help statewide, and Provo, Utah County cities and Ogden add 0% deferred loans. Compare terms.</article>

items.title: Arizona Home Plus: Down Payment Assistance Forgiven After 5 Years
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Arizona's Home Plus program offers up to 4% of your loan in down payment help, forgiven after 60 months if its terms are met. No first-time buyer rule; credit and income requirements apply.</article>

items.title: Virginia Housing (VHDA) Down Payment Assistance: Grants and Plus Second Mortgage
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Virginia Housing gives first-time buyers a down payment grant of 2.5% (FHA) or 2% (conventional) that's never repaid, or a Plus Second Mortgage with monthly repayment.</article>

items.title: Oregon Flex Lending: FirstHome, NextStep and Down Payment Assistance
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Oregon's Flex Lending pairs FirstHome and NextStep loans with down payment assistance of 4% of the loan (5% for some households), forgivable or repayable by income.</article>

items.title: OHFA Down Payment Assistance: Ohio Home Buyer Programs Explained
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>OHFA gives Ohio buyers 3% to 3.5% of the price as a 0% second loan, plus lower rates for recent grads, teachers, nurses and first responders. See who qualifies.</article>

items.title: CHFA Down Payment Assistance: Colorado Grants and Loans Explained
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>CHFA offers Colorado buyers a grant of up to 3% or a deferred second loan of up to 4% of the mortgage, each capped at $25,000. Compare programs and requirements.</article>

items.title: WHEDA Loans: Wisconsin Low Down Payment Mortgages and Assistance
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>WHEDA's Advantage loans pair with Easy Close DPA, up to 6% of the purchase price, to cover your down payment and closing costs. See requirements and how to apply.</article>

items.title: Home Buyer Programs for Teachers, Nurses and First Responders by State
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Five states give teachers, nurses, police, firefighters and EMTs extra down payment help or a lower rate. Compare amounts, who qualifies and how each program is repaid.</article>

items.title: MSHDA MI Home Loan and MI 10K DPA: Michigan Down Payment Help
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Michigan's MSHDA MI Home Loan can be paired with up to $10,000 in MI 10K down payment assistance, an interest-free second loan you repay when you sell, refinance or pay off the first mortgage.</article>

items.title: Maryland Mortgage Program (MMP): Who Qualifies and How Much You Can Get
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>The Maryland Mortgage Program offers $6,000 or 3% to 5% of your loan as a 0% deferred second loan. See who qualifies, MMP rates published Nov. 13, 2026 and how to apply.</article>

items.title: THDA Great Choice Home Loan: Tennessee Down Payment Help Explained
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>THDA's Great Choice loan offers a 30-year fixed rate plus down payment help: up to $10,000 with no payments or up to $15,000 repaid monthly. See who qualifies.</article>

items.title: Some Lenders Offer 2027 Loan Limits Up to $850,000 Before FHFA Acts. What It Means for Buyers
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>FHFA hasn't announced 2027 conforming loan limits yet, but some lenders already lend up to $850,000. Here's what buyers near the current $832,750 limit should know.</article>

items.title: Nearly 4 Million Homeowners Over 75 Still Have a Mortgage. What That Means for Your Parents
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>A new Realtor.com analysis finds 3.93 million homeowners age 75 and older carry a mortgage. Here's what happens to that loan if a parent sells, moves or passes away.</article>

items.title: Builders Cut Prices at Record Pace as Confidence Hits 14-Year Low. What It Means for Buyers
items.author: Alex Lange
items.content: <article>Nearly half of home builders cut prices in November as builder confidence fell to its lowest level since 2012. Here's how buyers of new homes can use that leverage.</article>
